title: Operator sending domain: notify.anth.us through the newsletter's sending stack
description:
**Reworked 2026-11-04:** Ryan reversed the architecture. No new AWS account and no central service; see docs/notifications-plan.md in AnthusAI/Caducus.

**Milestone:** M1, first slice

**Goal.** Operator mail gets its own domain and configuration set in papyrus-production, using the sending stack sites already use rather than a second template. SES there already has production access, so nothing needs verifying per recipient.

**Build.**
- `infra/newsletter/papyrus-newsletter-sending.yaml`: add parameter `EventTransport` (`sns`, `eventbridge`, `both`; default `sns`, so existing stacks do not change). `eventbridge` adds the EventBridge destination for SEND, DELIVERY, BOUNCE, COMPLAINT, REJECT, DELIVERY_DELAY and omits the SNS topic. Check that CloudFormation's event-destination resource takes the EventBridge property; if not, a small custom resource.
- Deploy `papyrus-newsletter-sending-operators`: SiteId `operators`, SendingDomain `notify.anth.us`, the anth.us zone in this same account, so no delegation. A read on 2026-11-04 shows no `notify` records and no collision. Creates `_dmarc.notify.anth.us`. Separately worth knowing: the apex anth.us zone shows no `_dmarc` record.
- Configuration set `papyrus-operators`: never OPEN or CLICK, and a test on the template fails if either appears. `infra/newsletter/README.md` updated.

**Acceptance.**
`aws sesv2 get-email-identity --email-identity notify.anth.us` reads `True SUCCESS SUCCESS`; simulator send shows an `Email Delivered` event on the default bus.

**Depends on:** PPY-d21c7f
**Related:** kanbus-06de58
